source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ מָלַ֣ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְהוֹעַדָּ֖ן מִירוּשָׁלָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] son of twenty and five year[s] became king Amaziah, and twenty and nine year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

en.L: Amaziah [was] twenty-five years old [when] he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
en.B: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.
en.R: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the opening formula of 2 Kings 14:2, without the date of 14:1
decisions.reason: Chapter 25 retells the reign of Amaziah from 2 Kings 14:1-20. Kings first dates his accession by the reign of Joash king of Israel (14:1); Chronicles leaves the date out, as it usually does with the kings of the north, and names Amaziah in this verse instead of saying "he". The rest of the verse is the same as 2 Kings 14:2. There the written consonants spell the mother's name Jehoaddin and the form read aloud Jehoaddan; Chronicles has Jehoaddan. It is the same woman.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-five years: twenty-five years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years, as in 2 Kings 14:2.

decisions.choice: the name of his mother: the queen mother
decisions.reason: Kings and Chronicles name the mother of each king of Judah, who held an honored place at court.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 14:2
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the wording it uses at 2 Kings 14:2, with the name Amaziah where Chronicles has it. Literal adds "when" in brackets, since the Hebrew here has no word for "he was".

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה רַ֕ק לֹ֖א בְּלֵבָ֥ב שָׁלֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, only not with a heart whole.

en.L: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, only not with a whole heart.
en.B: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, yet not with a whole heart.
en.R: Amaziah did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, but he did not do it with all his heart.

decisions.choice: not with a whole heart: in place of the comparison with David and Joash
decisions.reason: The first half is the same as 2 Kings 14:3. Kings goes on to say that Amaziah was not like David but did as his father Joash had done, and that the high places stayed (14:3-4). Chronicles says instead that he did right "only not with a whole heart", and leaves out the high places.

decisions.choice: a whole heart: undivided loyalty
decisions.reason: A "whole" or complete heart is loyalty given fully and without holding back, the heart David asked for Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:9; 29:19) and that Asa had (2 Chronicles 15:17).

decisions.choice: a divided heart that shows itself later
decisions.reason: The note prepares for the rest of the chapter: Amaziah obeys the prophet once (verses 7-10) but then worships the gods of Edom (verse 14) and turns from Yahweh (verse 27).

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The good verdict is worded the same way at each level throughout these books, as in 2 Kings 14:3. Readable names Amaziah and says "with all his heart" for the idiom (m2).

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר חָזְקָ֥ה הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַֽיַּהֲרֹג֙ אֶת־עֲבָדָ֔יו הַמַּכִּ֖ים אֶת־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when was strong the kingdom upon him, and he killed his servants, the [ones] striking down the king his father.

en.L: And it happened, as soon as the kingdom was firm upon him, that he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.
en.B: As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his control, he executed the officials who had murdered his father the king.
en.R: As soon as Amaziah had firm control of the kingdom, he put to death the officials who had killed his father, the king.

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 14:5, with two small changes
decisions.reason: Kings says the kingdom was firm "in his hand" and that he "struck down" the killers; Chronicles says the kingdom was firm "upon him" and that he "killed" them. The sense is the same: once his rule was secure, he put his father's murderers to death.

decisions.choice: the officials who had struck down the king: Zabad and Jehozabad
decisions.reason: These are the two officials who killed Joash in his bed (24:25-26).

decisions.choice: officials; executed ... murdered (Balanced); put to death ... killed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep their wording of 2 Kings 14:5. These were royal officials, so Balanced and Readable call them officials, as these books do for a king's servants at court. Balanced uses "executed" for the punishment and "murdered" for the crime.

source.text: וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א הֵמִ֑ית כִּ֣י כַכָּת֣וּב בַּתּוֹרָ֡ה בְּסֵ֣פֶר מֹשֶׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא־יָמ֨וּתוּ אָב֤וֹת עַל־בָּנִים֙ וּבָנִים֙ לֹא־יָמ֣וּתוּ עַל־אָב֔וֹת כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יָמֽוּתוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And their sons not he put to death, but according to [what is] written in the law, in [the] book of Moses, which commanded Yahweh, saying, Not will die fathers on account of sons, and sons not will die on account of fathers, but [each] man for his sin they will die.

en.L: But their {{gender:children|sons}} he did not put to death, but [did] according to what is written in the law, in the book of Moses, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded, saying, "{{gender:Parents|Fathers}} shall not die for {{gender:children|sons}}, and {{gender:children|sons}} shall not die for {{gender:parents|fathers}}; but each shall die for {{gender:their|his}} own sin."
en.B: But he did not put their {{gender:children|sons}} to death. In this he followed the law as it stands written in the book of Moses, in which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave this command: "{{gender:Parents|Fathers}} are not to die for their {{gender:children|sons}}, nor {{gender:children|sons}} for their {{gender:parents|fathers}}. Each one is to die only for {{gender:their|his}} own sin."
en.R: But he did not kill their {{gender:children|sons}}. He obeyed what is written in the law, in the book of Moses. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded, "Do not put {{gender:parents|fathers}} to death for what their {{gender:children|sons}} have done. Do not put {{gender:children|sons}} to death for what their {{gender:parents|fathers}} have done. People may be put to death only for their own sin."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Deuteronomy 24:16, as in 2 Kings 14:6
decisions.reason: The law quoted is Deuteronomy 24:16. Deuteronomy and Kings say "shall be put to death"; Chronicles uses the plain verb "shall die" all three times. In a law about punishment it means the same thing: no one is to be executed for another's crime. Like Kings, Chronicles adds "but" before the last clause; like Deuteronomy, it keeps the last verb plural ("they shall die").

decisions.choice: in the law, in the book of Moses
decisions.reason: Kings says "in the book of the law of Moses" (2 Kings 14:6); Chronicles says "in the law, in the book of Moses". Both name the written law Moses gave (Deuteronomy 31:9, 24-26).

decisions.choice: sons ... fathers: children and parents
decisions.reason: In the law the words cover parents and children of either sex, as in Deuteronomy 24:16. "Their sons" are the killers' children, named with the same word the law uses.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 14:6; "die" at Literal and Balanced; Parents / children; their
decisions.reason: Each level follows its wording of 2 Kings 14:6 and Deuteronomy 24:16. Literal and Balanced say "die" where Chronicles has the plain verb (m1); Readable keeps "put to death", which is what the verb means here. The gender setting gives "parents", "children" and "their" by default and "fathers", "sons" and "his" as the alternative (m3). Literal supplies "did" after the second "but".

source.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֣ם לְבֵית־אָב֗וֹת לְשָׂרֵ֤י הָאֲלָפִים֙ וּלְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֔וֹת לְכָל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן וַֽיִּפְקְדֵ֗ם לְמִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וַיִּמְצָאֵ֗ם שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֤לֶף בָּחוּר֙ יוֹצֵ֣א צָבָ֔א אֹחֵ֖ז רֹ֥מַח וְצִנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered Amaziah Judah and set them by house of fathers, by commanders of the thousands and by commanders of the hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin; and he mustered them from [a] son of twenty year[s] and upward, and he found them three hundred thousand chosen, going out [to the] army, holding spear and large shield.

en.L: And Amaziah gathered Judah and set them by fathers' houses, under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. And he mustered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them [to be] 300,000 chosen [men], going out [to the] army, handling spear and large shield.
en.B: Amaziah assembled the men of Judah and organized them by their ancestral families under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered those twenty years old and over and found 300,000 chosen men fit for war, able to handle spear and large shield.
en.R: Amaziah called together the men of Judah. He arranged them by families and put commanders over units of a thousand and units of a hundred. He did this for all Judah and Benjamin. Then he counted the men who were twenty years old or older. There were 300,000 of the best soldiers, ready for war and able to fight with spear and large shield.

decisions.choice: by fathers' houses, under commanders of thousands and of hundreds
decisions.reason: The army was raised and led through the family structure of the tribes, each ancestral family supplying men under officers over units of a thousand and of a hundred, as in Numbers 1:2 and 31:14. This muster is not in Kings.

decisions.choice: mustered from twenty years old: counted for military service
decisions.reason: The verb means to count and enroll men for the army. Twenty was the age for service in the census of Numbers 1:3. On the size of numbers given in thousands, see the note at Numbers 1:21; here, as there, the text is read as giving the number.

decisions.choice: spear and large shield: heavy infantry
decisions.reason: The large shield covered the whole body and was carried with a spear by soldiers who fought in close ranks, as in 14:7.

decisions.choice: chosen, going out to the army: picked men fit for war
decisions.reason: "Chosen" names men picked for their fitness (13:3). "Going out to the army" means able to go to war, as in Numbers 1:3.

decisions.choice: ancestral families (Balanced), families (Readable); men; the best soldiers
decisions.reason: "Fathers' houses" is "ancestral families" at Balanced and "families" at Readable, as in the earlier books. Balanced and Readable add "men" to the muster, and Readable says "the best soldiers" for the chosen men.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂכֹּ֣ר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵ֥אָה אֶ֛לֶף גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל בְּמֵאָ֥ה כִכַּר־כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And he hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty [men] of valor for one hundred talent[s] of silver.

en.L: And he hired from Israel 100,000 mighty [men] of valor for 100 talents of silver.
en.B: He also hired 100,000 mighty warriors from Israel for {{units:about 7,500 pounds of silver|100 talents of silver}}.
en.R: He also paid {{units:about 7,500 pounds of silver|100 talents of silver}} to hire 100,000 brave warriors from Israel.

decisions.choice: Israel: the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Here "Israel" is the kingdom of the north, ruled from Samaria, as the man of God makes clear in verse 7 by calling them "the sons of Ephraim".

decisions.choice: hired for 100 talents: paid soldiers
decisions.reason: Amaziah paid the king of Israel or the soldiers themselves to fight for him. A talent was a large weight of metal, about 75 pounds, so the price was very great.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: tried fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase names strong, capable warriors, as in 13:3 and 14:7.

decisions.choice: about 7,500 pounds of silver / 100 talents of silver
decisions.reason: The units setting gives the weight in pounds by default and in talents as the alternative; a talent is about 75 pounds. Literal keeps "100 talents".

source.text: וְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים בָּ֤א אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַמֶּ֕לֶךְ אַל־יָבֹ֥א עִמְּךָ֖ צְבָ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין יְהוָה֙ עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] man of the God came to him, saying, O king, let not go with you [the] army of Israel, for not [is] Yahweh with Israel, all [the] sons of Ephraim.

en.L: And a man of God came to him, saying, "O king, let not the army of Israel go with you, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] not with Israel, all the sons of Ephraim.
en.B: But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, the army of Israel must not go with you, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not with Israel, with any of the people of Ephraim.
en.R: But a man of God came to Amaziah and said, "Your Majesty, do not let the army from Israel go with you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is not with Israel, with any of those people from Ephraim.

decisions.choice: a man of God: a prophet
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet who speaks for God (1 Samuel 2:27; 1 Kings 13:1). He is not named.

decisions.choice: Yahweh is not with Israel
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom had left Yahweh for the calves of Jeroboam (13:8-9). To fight with its army would be to lean on people Yahweh was not with, and the battle would be lost (verse 8). Chronicles teaches the same lesson in 16:7-9 and 19:2.

decisions.choice: all the sons of Ephraim: the northern kingdom by its leading tribe
decisions.reason: Ephraim was the strongest tribe of the north, and its name stands for the whole northern kingdom (Isaiah 7:2; Hosea 5:3).

decisions.choice: O king (Balanced); Your Majesty (Readable); the people of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Readable uses the modern form of address to a king. "Sons of Ephraim" is "people of Ephraim" at Balanced and Readable, since a whole people is meant. The speech goes on in verse 8.

source.text: כִּ֚י אִם־בֹּ֣א אַתָּ֔ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה חֲזַ֣ק לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה יַכְשִֽׁילְךָ֤ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֔ב כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־כֹּ֛חַ בֵּאלֹהִ֖ים לַעְז֥וֹר וּלְהַכְשִֽׁיל׃

records.literal_gloss: But if go you, act, be strong for the battle, will make stumble you the God before [the] enemy, for there [is] power in God to help and to make stumble.

en.L: But if you go, act, be strong for the battle, God will make you stumble before [the] enemy; for there is power in God to help and to make [one] stumble."
en.B: Even if you go and fight, and are strong in battle, God will cast you down before the enemy, for God has power to help and to cast down."
en.R: If you go anyway and fight bravely, God will let your enemy defeat you. God has the power to help, and the power to make people fall."

decisions.choice: if you go, act, be strong: even if you fight bravely, you will lose
alternatives: but go yourself, act, be strong for battle (a call to go without the hired troops)
if you think to be strong by these
decisions.reason: The commands "act, be strong" are said with irony: however bravely Amaziah fights with the hired army, God will bring him down. The Greek translation and some interpreters read the line differently, as "if you think to be strong with these", which changes a few letters; the sense of the warning is the same.

decisions.choice: God has power to help and to cast down
decisions.reason: The outcome of the battle lies with God, not with the size of the army, a lesson Chronicles teaches often (14:10; 20:6; 1 Chronicles 29:12). The same verb, "make stumble", ends both halves of the verse.

decisions.choice: make you stumble before the enemy: give you defeat
decisions.reason: To stumble or fall before an enemy is to be beaten by him in battle (Leviticus 26:37).

decisions.choice: cast down (Balanced); let your enemy defeat you; make people fall (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses one verb for both uses of the Hebrew verb, as the Hebrew does. Readable says plainly what the warning means. Balanced and Readable render the commands as an "even if" or "anyway" clause, following m1.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמַֽה־לַּעֲשׂוֹת֙ לִמְאַ֣ת הַכִּכָּ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִגְד֣וּד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים יֵ֚שׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ הַרְבֵּ֥ה מִזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Amaziah to [the] man of the God, And what [is there] to do for the hundred talent[s] which I have given to [the] troop of Israel? And said [the] man of the God, There is to Yahweh to give to you much more than this.

en.L: And Amaziah said to the man of God, "And what [is there] to do about the 100 talents that I have given to the troop of Israel?" And the man of God said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has [the means] to give you much more than this."
en.B: Amaziah asked the man of God, "But what about the silver I have paid to the troops of Israel, the {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}}?" The man of God answered, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is able to give you much more than that."
en.R: Amaziah asked the man of God, "But what about all the silver I paid to the soldiers from Israel? It was {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}}!" The man of God answered, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} can give you much more than that."

decisions.choice: the troop of Israel: the hired band
decisions.reason: The word names a band or troop of soldiers, often raiders. It is used of the hired men from Israel through verse 13.

decisions.choice: there is to Yahweh to give you more: Yahweh is able to give you more
decisions.reason: "There is to" someone to do a thing means he is able to do it. The man of God tells Amaziah that the loss of the silver is small beside what Yahweh can give him for obeying.

decisions.choice: the silver ... about 7,500 pounds / 100 talents
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the silver (the talents of verse 6) and give the weight with the units setting. Literal keeps "100 talents".

source.text: וַיַּבְדִּילֵ֣ם אֲמַצְיָ֗הוּ לְהַגְּדוּד֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤א אֵלָיו֙ מֵֽאֶפְרַ֔יִם לָלֶ֖כֶת לִמְקוֹמָ֑ם וַיִּ֨חַר אַפָּ֤ם מְאֹד֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וַיָּשׁ֥וּבוּ לִמְקוֹמָ֖ם בָּחֳרִי־אָֽף׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And separated them Amaziah, the troop which had come to him from Ephraim, to go to their place; and burned their anger greatly against Judah, and they returned to their place in heat of anger.

en.L: And Amaziah separated them, the troop that had come to him from Ephraim, to go to their place. And their anger burned greatly against Judah, and they returned to their place in burning anger.
en.B: So Amaziah released the troops who had joined him from Ephraim and sent them home. They were furious with Judah, and they went home in a blazing rage.
en.R: So Amaziah sent away the soldiers who had come to him from Ephraim and told them to go home. They became very angry with Judah, and they went home in a rage.

decisions.choice: separated them to go to their place: dismissed them and sent them home
decisions.reason: Amaziah set the hired men apart from his own army and sent them back to their own land. He obeyed the man of God, though it cost him the silver.

decisions.choice: their anger burned; in heat of anger: great rage
decisions.reason: Hebrew pictures anger as heat or burning. Sent home, the soldiers lost their share of the plunder of war, and they took the dismissal as an insult. Their anger leads to the raid of verse 13.

decisions.choice: sent them home; went home
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "home" for "their place".

source.text: וַאֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔ק וַיִּנְהַג֙ אֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ גֵּ֣יא הַמֶּ֑לַח וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־בְּנֵי־שֵׂעִ֖יר עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Amaziah strengthened himself and led out his people and went [to the] Valley of Salt and struck down [the] sons of Seir, ten thousand.

en.L: And Amaziah strengthened himself and led out his people, and went [to] the Valley of Salt and struck down the sons of Seir, 10,000.
en.B: Then Amaziah took courage and led out his troops. He went to the Valley of Salt and struck down 10,000 of the people of Seir.
en.R: Then Amaziah gathered his courage and led his army out to the Valley of Salt. There he killed 10,000 of the people of Seir, that is, the Edomites.

decisions.choice: the battle of 2 Kings 14:7, told at more length
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 14:7 says Amaziah "struck down Edom in the Valley of Salt, ten thousand" and took Sela. Chronicles calls the enemy "the sons of Seir" and goes on in verse 12 with the 10,000 taken alive. The Valley of Salt, probably near the south end of the Dead Sea, is where David had defeated Edom (1 Chronicles 18:12).

decisions.choice: the sons of Seir: the Edomites
decisions.reason: Seir is the hill country of Edom, and "the sons of Seir" are its people (Genesis 36:8-9; 2 Chronicles 20:10). Verse 14 calls them "the Edomites".

decisions.choice: strengthened himself; his people: took courage; his army
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather strength or courage, here after sending away a fifth of his force. "His people" are his troops, as often when an army is in the field.

decisions.choice: his people / his troops / his army; the people of Seir
decisions.reason: The army in the field is "the people" at Literal, "the troops" at Balanced and "the army" at Readable. Readable adds "that is, the Edomites" so the reader knows who Seir's people are (m2).

source.text: וַעֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֜ים חַיִּ֗ים שָׁבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְבִיא֖וּם לְרֹ֣אשׁ הַסָּ֑לַע וַיַּשְׁלִיכ֛וּם מֵֽרֹאשׁ־הַסֶּ֖לַע וְכֻלָּ֥ם נִבְקָֽעוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And ten thousand alive took captive [the] sons of Judah, and they brought them to [the] top of the rock and threw them from [the] top of the rock, and all of them were split open.

en.L: And 10,000 alive the sons of Judah took captive, and they brought them to the top of the rock and threw them down from the top of the rock, and all of them were burst open.
en.B: The men of Judah also captured 10,000 alive. They took them up to the top of the rock and hurled them down from there, and all of them were dashed to pieces.
en.R: The soldiers of Judah also took 10,000 men alive. They led them up to the top of the rock and threw them off it, and all of them were smashed to pieces on the ground below.

decisions.choice: the rock: perhaps Sela, the Edomite stronghold
decisions.reason: The word means "rock" or "cliff". With the article it may be the place called Sela, "the Rock", which 2 Kings 14:7 says Amaziah captured in this campaign; or it may be any high cliff in the rocky land of Edom.

decisions.choice: 10,000 alive: a second group, not the 10,000 killed
decisions.reason: Verse 11 counts the dead; this verse adds 10,000 taken prisoner and then put to death. Such killing of prisoners was a known cruelty of war in that age (Amos 1:13; Psalm 137:9), and the writer reports it without comment.

decisions.choice: were split open: were dashed to pieces
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or burst open, of bodies broken by the fall.

decisions.choice: the men of Judah (Balanced), the soldiers of Judah (Readable); dashed / smashed to pieces
decisions.reason: "The sons of Judah" here are Amaziah's soldiers, all men, so no gender setting is used. Readable says "on the ground below" to make the picture plain.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י הַגְּד֗וּד אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵשִׁ֤יב אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מִלֶּ֤כֶת עִמּוֹ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיִּפְשְׁטוּ֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מִשֹּׁמְר֖וֹן וְעַד־בֵּ֣ית חוֹר֑וֹן וַיַּכּ֤וּ מֵהֶם֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖זּוּ בִּזָּ֥ה רַבָּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of the troop which had turned back Amaziah from going with him to the battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria and to Beth-horon, and struck down of them three thousand, and they plundered plunder much.

en.L: And the sons of the troop that Amaziah had turned back from going with him to the battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon, and struck down of them 3,000, and plundered much plunder.
en.B: Meanwhile the troops whom Amaziah had sent back, not letting them go with him into battle, raided the towns of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon. They killed 3,000 people and carried off a great deal of plunder.
en.R: Meanwhile, the soldiers Amaziah had sent home instead of taking them to battle attacked the towns of Judah, all the way from Samaria to Beth-horon. They killed 3,000 people and took away many valuable things.

decisions.choice: and the sons of the troop raided: at the same time as the campaign
decisions.reason: The sentence turns from Amaziah to the hired men; the order of the Hebrew suggests their raid took place while Amaziah was away fighting Edom. It is the price of his first trust in hired soldiers.

decisions.choice: from Samaria to Beth-horon
decisions.reason: Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom; Beth-horon lay on the border between Ephraim and Benjamin, northwest of Jerusalem (Joshua 16:3, 5). The raiders seem to have set out from Samaria and struck the towns of Judah along the northern border as far as Beth-horon. The exact route is not clear.

decisions.choice: the sons of the troop: the members of the band
decisions.reason: "Sons of" names those who belong to a group, here the hired soldiers of verses 6-10.

decisions.choice: Meanwhile; people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "meanwhile" for the timing the Hebrew implies (m1), and say "people" for those killed, whom the Hebrew calls "of them".

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵ֨י ב֤וֹא אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵֽהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת־אֲדוֹמִ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֗א אֶת־אֱלֹהֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י שֵׂעִ֔יר וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֥ם ל֖וֹ לֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְלִפְנֵיהֶ֥ם יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה וְלָהֶ֥ם יְקַטֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after came Amaziah from striking down the Edomites, and he brought [the] gods of [the] sons of Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and before them he bowed down, and to them he made smoke.

en.L: And it happened, after Amaziah came from striking down the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and before them he bowed down, and to them he burned incense.
en.B: After Amaziah came back from defeating the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the people of Seir and set them up as his own gods. He bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
en.R: When Amaziah came back from defeating the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir home with him. He set them up as his own gods. He bowed down to worship them, and he burned incense to them.

decisions.choice: he set up the gods of the defeated people as his own gods
decisions.reason: Conquerors often carried off the images of a beaten people's gods as trophies. Amaziah went further and worshiped them, though they had not saved their own people from him. The prophet makes that point in verse 15. This is the fruit of the divided heart of verse 2, and it is not in Kings.

decisions.choice: bowed down; made smoke: worshiped and offered to them
decisions.reason: Bowing down is the act of worship. "Made smoke" is the verb for burning incense or offerings, as in 2 Kings 14:4.

decisions.choice: bowed down to worship them
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to worship" to make clear that the bowing was an act of worship (m2).

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בַּאֲמַצְיָ֑הוּ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵלָיו֙ נָבִ֔יא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לָ֤מָּה דָרַ֨שְׁתָּ֙ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־עַמָּ֖ם מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Amaziah, and he sent to him a prophet, and he said to him, Why have you sought the gods of the people which not delivered their people from your hand?

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Amaziah, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent to him a prophet, and he said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of the people, which did not deliver their [own] people from your hand?"
en.B: So the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Amaziah, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent a prophet to him, who said, "Why have you sought the gods of this people, gods that could not rescue their own people from your hand?"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with Amaziah. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent a prophet to him, who said, "Why have you turned to these gods? They could not even save their own people from you!"

decisions.choice: sought: turned to for help and worshiped
decisions.reason: To "seek" a god is to turn to him in worship and ask his help. Chronicles uses the word often for seeking Yahweh (1 Chronicles 16:11; 2 Chronicles 15:2). Here it is used of the gods of Edom, again in verse 20.

decisions.choice: gods that did not deliver their own people
decisions.reason: The prophet points out the folly: the gods of Edom could not save Edom from Amaziah, so they could not save Amaziah. Compare the same argument in 32:13-15 and Isaiah 36:18-20, where it is turned against Yahweh.

decisions.choice: the anger of Yahweh burned: Yahweh was very angry
decisions.reason: Hebrew pictures anger as burning, as of the soldiers in verse 10.

decisions.choice: sought (Balanced), turned to (Readable); could not rescue / save
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "sought" so the link with verse 20 and with seeking Yahweh stays clear; Readable says "turned to". "Could not" makes clear that the gods failed to deliver their people.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בְּדַבְּר֣וֹ אֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַלְיוֹעֵ֤ץ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ נְתַנּ֔וּךָ חֲדַל־לְךָ֖ לָ֣מָּה יַכּ֑וּךָ וַיֶּחְדַּ֣ל הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־יָעַ֤ץ אֱלֹהִים֙ לְהַשְׁחִיתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּ֔את וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ לַעֲצָתִֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as he was speaking to him, and he said to him, Have [as] counselor to the king we appointed you? Stop for yourself; why should they strike you down? And stopped the prophet and said, I know that has counseled God to destroy you, because you have done this and not listened to my counsel.

en.L: And it happened, as he was speaking to him, that he said to him, "Have we made you counselor to the king? Stop! Why should they strike you down?" And the prophet stopped, and he said, "I know that God has counseled to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
en.B: While the prophet was still speaking, the king said to him, "Have we made you the king's counselor? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" So the prophet stopped, but he added, "I know that God has decided to destroy you, since you have done this and refused to listen to my counsel."
en.R: But while the prophet was still speaking, the king said to him, "Did we make you an adviser to the king? Stop! Do you want to be killed?" So the prophet said no more, except this: "I know that God has decided to destroy you. You have done this, and you have not listened to my advice."

decisions.choice: have we made you the king's counselor?: who asked your advice?
decisions.reason: The question is scornful. Amaziah says the prophet has no place at court to give the king advice. "We" is the king speaking for his court.

decisions.choice: stop! why should they strike you down?: a threat
decisions.reason: The king orders the prophet to be silent and warns that he may be killed if he goes on. "They" are the king's men; the verb has no named subject. Joash had a prophet stoned for such words (24:20-22).

decisions.choice: counselor ... has counseled ... my counsel: a play on one word
decisions.reason: The same root runs through the verse and into verse 17. Amaziah refuses the prophet as a counselor; the prophet answers that God has "counseled", that is, decided, Amaziah's ruin, because he would not take God's counsel. In verse 17 Amaziah takes counsel elsewhere, and it leads to his defeat.

decisions.choice: has counseled (Literal); has decided (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated word to show the play on it (m3); Balanced and Readable say what it means here. Balanced makes "they strike you" passive, and Readable turns the threat into a plain question.

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶל־יוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן־יְהוֹאָחָ֧ז בֶּן־יֵה֛וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכָ֖ה נִתְרָאֶ֥ה פָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And took counsel Amaziah king of Judah and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look at one another [in the] face.

en.L: And Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."
en.B: Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, let us meet face to face."
en.R: Then Amaziah king of Judah talked with his advisers. He sent a message to Joash king of Israel, the son of Jehoahaz and grandson of Jehu. It said, "Come out and face me in battle."

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 14:8, with "took counsel"
decisions.reason: The challenge is the same as in 2 Kings 14:8. Chronicles opens with "Amaziah took counsel", which carries on the play on "counsel" from verse 16: having rejected God's counsel, he took advice from others. It leaves out "messengers" and spells the king of Israel's name Joash, the short form of Jehoash (see 2 Kings 14:1).

decisions.choice: let us look one another in the face: a challenge to fight
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:8, verse 21 shows what the words mean: the two kings meet in battle. Amaziah may also have been stirred by the raid of verse 13.

decisions.choice: meet face to face (Balanced); face me in battle (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 2 Kings 14:8. Readable says "talked with his advisers" for "took counsel".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל־אֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַח֜וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֗וֹן שָׁ֠לַח אֶל־הָאֶ֜רֶז אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּלְּבָנוֹן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָֽה־אֶת־בִּתְּךָ֥ לִבְנִ֖י לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲבֹ֞ר חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וַתִּרְמֹ֖ס אֶת־הַחֽוֹחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Joash king of Israel to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle which [was] in Lebanon sent to the cedar which [was] in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son for a wife; and passed by [the] beast of the field which [was] in Lebanon and trampled the thistle.

en.L: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle that [was] in Lebanon sent to the cedar that [was] in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And a wild animal of the field that [was] in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
en.B: Joash king of Israel sent back word to Amaziah king of Judah: "There was a thistle in Lebanon that sent word to a cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon came by and trampled the thistle.
en.R: Joash king of Israel sent this answer to Amaziah king of Judah: "Once a thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar tree in Lebanon. It said, 'Let your daughter marry my son.' But then a wild animal in Lebanon walked by and crushed the thistle under its feet.

decisions.choice: the fable of 2 Kings 14:9, word for word
decisions.reason: Joash's answer is the same as in 2 Kings 14:9, except that his name is spelled Joash here and Jehoash there.

decisions.choice: a fable: the thistle and the cedar
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:9, the thistle is Amaziah, small but asking to be treated as an equal by the great cedar, Israel. The wild animal passes by and crushes the thistle without effort. The speech goes on in verse 19.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 14:9
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of the fable in 2 Kings 14:9, including "thistle" and Readable's "Once".

source.text: אָמַ֗רְתָּ הִנֵּ֤ה הִכִּ֨יתָ֙ אֶת־אֱד֔וֹם וּנְשָׂאֲךָ֥ לִבְּךָ֖ לְהַכְבִּ֑יד עַתָּה֙ שְׁבָ֣ה בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ לָ֤מָּה תִתְגָּרֶה֙ בְּרָעָ֔ה וְנָ֣פַלְתָּ֔ אַתָּ֖ה וִיהוּדָ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: You have said, Look, you have struck down Edom, and has lifted you your heart to seek honor; now stay in your house; why should you stir up strife with evil, and you will fall, you and Judah with you?

en.L: You have said, 'Look, you have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up to seek glory. Now stay in your house. Why should you stir up trouble to your harm, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
en.B: You tell yourself that you have defeated Edom, and your heart has made you proud and eager for glory. Now stay at home. Why stir up trouble that will only bring you down, you and Judah with you?"
en.R: You say to yourself, 'Look, I have beaten Edom!' Now you are proud and want people to praise you. But stay at home. Why ask for trouble? You will fall, and Judah will fall with you."

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 14:10, with small changes
decisions.reason: Kings has "You have indeed struck down Edom ... be honored and stay in your house". Chronicles has "You have said, 'Look, you have struck down Edom'": Joash mocks Amaziah's boast. In place of "be honored" it has "to seek honor", and it adds "now". The rest is the same.

decisions.choice: your heart has lifted you up to seek honor: pride drives you to look for more glory
decisions.reason: The heart lifting someone up is a picture of pride, as in 2 Kings 14:10 and Deuteronomy 8:14. Amaziah wants more glory than the victory over Edom gave him.

decisions.choice: stir up strife to your harm
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:10, the verb means to provoke a fight, and "with evil" means trouble that will turn into disaster for the one who starts it.

decisions.choice: You tell yourself (Balanced); You say to yourself, 'I have beaten Edom!' (Readable)
decisions.reason: "You have said" means what Amaziah says in his own mind or to others. Readable puts the boast in Amaziah's own words. The rest of each level keeps its wording of 2 Kings 14:10.

source.text: וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֣ע אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ כִּ֤י מֵהָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ הִ֔יא לְמַ֖עַן תִּתָּ֣ם בְּיָ֑ד כִּ֣י דָֽרְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And not listened Amaziah, for from the God it [was], in order to give them into [the] hand, because they had sought [the] gods of Edom.

en.L: But Amaziah did not listen, for it [was] from God, in order to give them into [the] hand [of their enemy], because they had sought the gods of Edom.
en.B: But Amaziah would not listen, for this came from God, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might hand them over to their enemy, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
en.R: But Amaziah would not listen. God had caused this, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could let their enemy defeat them, because they had turned to the gods of Edom.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 14:11 begins the same way; the rest is added
decisions.reason: Kings says only "Amaziah did not listen". Chronicles adds the reason: God was at work in Amaziah's stubbornness to punish the worship of Edom's gods. A like note is made about Rehoboam's refusal to listen (10:15).

decisions.choice: it was from God: God used the king's pride to bring judgment
decisions.reason: The writer does not excuse Amaziah; the prophet had already warned him (verse 16). God gave the king over to his own choice as the way judgment would come.

decisions.choice: give them into the hand: hand them over to the enemy
decisions.reason: "Give into the hand" means to give someone into an enemy's power. The enemy is not named; it is Joash and Israel.

decisions.choice: [of their enemy] / to their enemy
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the enemy in brackets; Balanced and Readable add it to complete the idiom (m3). Readable says "turned to" for "sought", as in verse 15.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַל יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּתְרָא֣וּ פָנִ֔ים ה֖וּא וַאֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה בְּבֵ֥ית שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Joash king of Israel, and they looked at one another [in the] face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh which [belongs] to Judah.

en.L: And Joash king of Israel went up, and they looked one another in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which [belongs] to Judah.
en.B: So Joash king of Israel went up against him, and the two kings, he and Amaziah king of Judah, met face to face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
en.R: So Joash king of Israel marched out with his army, and the two kings met in battle at Beth-shemesh, a town in Judah.

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 14:11, without "Amaziah did not listen"
decisions.reason: Kings begins this verse with Amaziah's refusal to listen; Chronicles has put that in verse 20, with its reason. The rest is the same, with the short form Joash for Jehoash.

decisions.choice: looked one another in the face: met in battle
decisions.reason: The words of Amaziah's challenge (verse 17) come true: the two kings face each other in battle.

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah
decisions.reason: Beth-shemesh was a town of Judah in the low hills west of Jerusalem (Joshua 15:10). Joash carried the war into Judah's own land.

decisions.choice: against him (Balanced); with his army; in battle (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 2 Kings 14:11.

source.text: וַיִּנָּ֥גֶף יְהוּדָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And was struck Judah before Israel, and they fled, each to his tents.

en.L: And Judah was struck down before Israel, and they fled, each to his tents.
en.B: Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his home.
en.R: Israel defeated Judah, and all the soldiers of Judah ran away to their homes.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Kings 14:12
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 14:12, where the written form and the form read aloud differ over "tent" or "tents"; here the plural stands in the text.

decisions.choice: fled each to his tents: the army broke up and went home
decisions.reason: "To his tents" is an old way of saying "home" (1 Samuel 4:10; 2 Samuel 18:17). Judah's army scattered.

decisions.choice: home (Balanced); homes (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 2 Kings 14:12, giving the plain sense of the idiom (m2).

source.text: וְאֵת֩ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֜ה בֶּן־יוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן־יְהוֹאָחָ֗ז תָּפַ֛שׂ יוֹאָ֥שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּבֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וַיְבִיאֵ֨הוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיִּפְרֹ֞ץ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם מִשַּׁ֤עַר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד־שַׁ֣עַר הַפּוֹנֶ֔ה אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Amaziah king of Judah son of Joash son of Jehoahaz seized Joash king of Israel at Beth-shemesh, and he brought him [to] Jerusalem, and broke into [the] wall of Jerusalem from [the] gate of Ephraim to [the] gate of the corner, four hundred cubit[s].

en.L: And Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, Joash king of Israel seized at Beth-shemesh; and he brought him [to] Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim up to the Corner Gate, 400 cubits.
en.B: Joash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah prisoner at Beth-shemesh; Amaziah was the son of Joash son of Jehoahaz. Then Joash brought him to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem along a stretch of {{units:about 600 feet|400 cubits}}, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
en.R: Joash king of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah at Beth-shemesh. (Amaziah was the son of Joash and grandson of Jehoahaz.) Then Joash took him to Jerusalem and broke down {{units:about 600 feet|400 cubits}} of the city wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 14:13, with three differences
decisions.reason: Kings calls Amaziah "son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah"; Chronicles has "son of Joash son of Jehoahaz", the names it uses for his father and grandfather (24:1; 21:17). Kings says Joash "came" to Jerusalem; Chronicles says he "brought him", that is, the captive Amaziah, to Jerusalem. And Kings has "at the Gate of Ephraim", Chronicles "from the Gate of Ephraim".

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz: the king also called Ahaziah
decisions.reason: Amaziah's grandfather is called Ahaziah in 22:1 and in Kings, and Jehoahaz in 21:17 and here. The two names have the same parts in reverse order, both meaning "Yahweh has taken hold".

decisions.choice: from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate: the north side of the wall
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:13. The Corner Gate is named here with a related word for "corner" (26:9 has the usual one). The north was the side most open to attack, and tearing down this stretch left Jerusalem without defense.

decisions.choice: about 600 feet / 400 cubits
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 2 Kings 14:13, with the names as Chronicles has them. The units setting gives the length in feet by default and in cubits as the alternative; Literal keeps "400 cubits".

source.text: וְכָֽל־הַזָּהָ֣ב וְהַכֶּ֡סֶף וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־הַ֠כֵּלִים הַנִּמְצְאִ֨ים בְּבֵית־הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים עִם־עֹבֵ֣ד אֱד֗וֹם וְאֶת־אֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י הַתַּֽעֲרֻב֑וֹת וַיָּ֖שָׁב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in [the] house of the God with Obed-edom, and [the] treasures of [the] house of the king, and [the] sons of the pledges; and he returned [to] Samaria.

en.L: And all the gold and the silver and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the house of the king, and the sons of the pledges [he took], and he returned [to] Samaria.
en.B: He carried off all the gold and silver, and every article that was found in the house of God in the care of Obed-edom, together with the palace treasures. He also took hostages, and then he returned to Samaria.
en.R: He took all the gold and silver and all the valuable objects he found in God's temple in the care of Obed-edom. He also took the treasures of the royal palace, and he took some people as hostages. Then he went back to Samaria.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 14:14, with "Obed-edom" added
decisions.reason: Kings begins "And he took all the gold ..."; Chronicles leaves out "he took", which the sense supplies. It says "the house of God" where Kings has "the house of Yahweh", "treasures" where Kings has "treasuries", and adds that the temple articles were "with Obed-edom".

decisions.choice: with Obed-edom: in the care of the family of gatekeepers
decisions.reason: Obed-edom was the head of a family of Levite gatekeepers, and the storehouses of the temple were given to his sons (1 Chronicles 26:4-8, 15). "With Obed-edom" most likely means the articles kept by that family, not a man then living.

decisions.choice: the sons of the pledges: hostages
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:14, people held in Samaria as pledges that Judah would keep the peace.

decisions.choice: [he took] / carried off / took
decisions.reason: Each level supplies the verb, as Kings has it, and keeps its wording of 2 Kings 14:14. Readable says "God's temple" for "the house of God".

source.text: וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־יוֹאָשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת יוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן־יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah after [the] death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen year[s].

en.L: And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.
en.B: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
en.R: Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen more years after Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, died.

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 14:17
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Kings 14:17, except that the king of Israel is named Joash, the short form of Jehoash. So both kings in the verse are called Joash: Amaziah's father, and the king of Israel who defeated him.

decisions.choice: the number of years moved forward
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:17, Balanced and Readable put "fifteen years" next to the verb; Literal keeps it at the end.

source.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הֲלֹא֙ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵי־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Amaziah, the first and the last, [are] not behold they written on [the] book of [the] kings of Judah and Israel?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Amaziah, the first and the last, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
en.R: Everything else Amaziah did, from beginning to end, is written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

decisions.choice: the source named: the book of the kings of Judah and Israel
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 14:18 points to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah". Chronicles adds "the first and the last" and names "the book of the kings of Judah and Israel", a work it cites for several kings of Judah (16:11; 27:7). It has not survived.

decisions.choice: are they not written?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: As throughout these books, the question means "they are written there". The Hebrew adds a word like "look" to point the reader to it.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As for every use of this formula: the question stays at Literal and becomes a statement at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: וּמֵעֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁר־סָ֤ר אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיָּ֣נָס לָכִ֑ישָׁה וַיִּשְׁלְח֤וּ אַחֲרָיו֙ לָכִ֔ישָׁה וַיְמִיתֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] time that turned aside Amaziah from after Yahweh, and they conspired against him a conspiracy in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.

en.L: And from the time that Amaziah turned aside from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they conspired a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
en.B: From the time Amaziah turned away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, some in Jerusalem formed a conspiracy against him, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
en.R: From the time Amaziah turned away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, some people in Jerusalem made a plot against him. So he ran away to the town of Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 14:19, with the cause of the plot added
decisions.reason: Kings says only that "they conspired against him in Jerusalem". Chronicles opens with "from the time that Amaziah turned aside from following Yahweh", tying the plot to his worship of Edom's gods (verse 14) and to the prophet's warning (verse 16). The rest of the verse is the same as Kings.

decisions.choice: from the time that: the plot grew from his turning away
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that the plotting began when Amaziah turned from Yahweh and went on until it killed him, which fits the long time between his defeat and his death (verse 25). It may also simply mark his turning as the cause of what followed.

decisions.choice: Lachish: a fortified city of Judah
decisions.reason: Lachish was one of Judah's strongest cities, southwest of Jerusalem (11:9).

decisions.choice: some in Jerusalem; sent men
decisions.reason: The plotters are not named. Balanced and Readable keep their wording of 2 Kings 14:19, saying "some" for the unnamed subject and adding "men", who were sent.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֖הוּ עַל־הַסּוּסִ֑ים וַֽיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֥יר יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they carried him on the horses and buried him with his fathers in [the] city of Judah.

en.L: And they carried him on the horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.
en.B: They brought his body back on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the city of Judah.
en.R: His body was carried back on horses, and he was buried with his ancestors in the city of Judah.

decisions.choice: the city of Judah, perhaps for "the City of David"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "the city of Judah", found nowhere else. 2 Kings 14:20 has "in Jerusalem ... in the City of David", and some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "the City of David" here. As it stands, "the city of Judah" would mean Judah's capital, Jerusalem. The text is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: carried him on the horses: brought the body home with honor
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 14:20, the king's body was brought back by horse. Though his own people had killed him, he was buried as a king.

decisions.choice: with his fathers: in the royal tombs
decisions.reason: To be buried with one's fathers is to be laid in the family grave, here the tombs of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "his body" for "him", since Amaziah was already dead, as in 2 Kings 14:20.
